title: Arakhin 10 - Why Not Sing Hallel on Purim, Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kipur?

chapters.title: Silver Trumpets and Instruments in the Bet HaMikdash
Opinions on Flute Players and Trumpet Blasts
The Twelve Days of Flutes and Hallel
Comparing Hallel on Sukkot, Pesach, and Shabbat
Why No Hallel on Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur, and Purim
Ancient Vessels of the Bet HaMikdash

summary: Rabbi Hidary goes through Masechet Arakhin on the rules of the silver trumpets, flutes, and other instruments played in the Bet HaMikdash, comparing the opinions of Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbanan on trumpet blasts. The class also examines the days of the year when Hallel is said, why Hallel is not said on Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur, and Purim, and concludes with historical details about the musical and ritual vessels of the Bet HaMikdash.
questions: How many trumpet blasts were played daily in the Bet HaMikdash?
Why do we say full Hallel on Sukkot but not on Pesach every day?
What is the difference between Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbanan regarding trumpet blasts?
Why do we not say Hallel on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur?
What are the reasons given for why Hallel is not said on Purim?
